_description: Fleet-wide evidence-completeness alert threshold for alerts/bsod-risk-prometheusrules.yaml's BSODRisk_FleetEvidenceIncomplete. Source of truth, bound by scripts/ci/validate-shared-thresholds.py. PromQL cannot read JSON at runtime, so the same value (divided by 100, since the recording rule is a 0-1 ratio -- see _units) is duplicated as a literal in that alert's expression -- same pattern as shared/host-contention-thresholds.json and shared/storage-latency-thresholds.json.
_why: Issue K (docs/info/peer-reviews/v0.19.0/issues/gitlab-issue-drafts-open-after-remediation.md): R-21 (v0.19.0) made per-VM evidence completeness ('of the checks we tried to run on this VM, how many actually reached a verdict') a first-class REPORTED axis in both bash and Python, but nothing exported it as a metric or made it ALERTABLE. A fleet whose guest-agent/exporter rollout stalls -- QGA disabled, windows_exporter never installed, VMs perpetually Halted -- degrades silently: every individual audit run still prints the gap correctly, but nobody is paged when the FLEET-WIDE figure crosses from 'a few VMs missing data' to 'most of the fleet is unassessed', because printing it once per manual run is not the same claim as monitoring it continuously.
_units: fleet_warn_below_pct itself is stored as percent (0-100) for human readability. The recording rule it binds to, bsod:fleet_evidence_completeness:ratio (alerts/bsod-risk-recording-rules.yaml), is a 0-1 RATIO -- sum(bsod_vm_checks_assessed) / sum(bsod_vm_checks_total) over every currently-reporting VM's raw per-VM counters, WEIGHTED by checks-per-VM, matching bsod:cluster_driver_compliance:ratio's own naming/unit convention. This now agrees with scripts/cnv-win-bsod-audit.sh --json's own summary.evidence_completeness_pct / insights-rules' fleet_summary.evidence_completeness_pct (also checks-weighted: sum of assessed / sum of total) BY CONSTRUCTION for the same input -- both are the identical statistic computed twice (once per audit run in bash/Python, once continuously via PromQL over the exporter's raw counters), not two different ones. (Revised 2026-08-04: an earlier version of this rule used an UNWEIGHTED avg() over a per-VM percent gauge, which disagreed with the audit script's own weighted figure whenever VMs had different check counts -- exporter's own module header documents the full reasoning.) The exporter (scripts/cnv-bsod-fleet-exporter.sh) still emits only per-VM gauges and does no fleet-level pre-aggregation itself, matching this repo's existing convention of deriving every other multi-VM aggregate (e.g. bsod:vmi_disk_latency:avg_1h) via a recording rule over raw per-entity data rather than a pre-computed collector-side statistic.
_fleet_warn_below_pct_note: A fleet whose checks-weighted evidence completeness drops below 80% means at least a fifth of the checks the framework tries to run, fleet-wide, are not reaching a verdict -- guest-side evidence (QGA, windows_exporter) is either not deployed broadly enough or is failing broadly enough that the framework's other alerts/gates are running mostly blind, not just gapped on a couple of VMs. This is a coverage/observability signal, not a BSOD-risk signal on its own -- it says 'we might be missing risk', not 'there is risk' -- so it is deliberately the framework's own lowest-severity alert tier (warning), never critical, and must never be conflated with the vm_risk_scores/risk_tier axis (which already scores UNKNOWN as 0, see risk-scoring.json's _why_unknown_is_zero).
_kcs_note: No KCS backing -- this is an [UNVALIDATED] operational-observability threshold (per CLAUDE.md's confidence-tier convention), not a BSOD-trigger claim. 80% is a reasoned starting point (four-fifths coverage is a common SRE-style floor for degraded-but-tolerable), not a value derived from a support case or measured fleet behavior.
_calibration_status: UNCALIBRATED (2026-08-04). No live fleet has been deliberately degraded (e.g. QGA stopped on a sample of VMs) and observed against this expression yet. TO CLOSE THIS: stop QGA on a known fraction of a test fleet's Windows VMs, confirm the exported bsod_vm_checks_assessed/_total per-VM series drop/shift for the affected VMs, confirm bsod:fleet_evidence_completeness:ratio drops proportionally, confirm BSODRisk_FleetEvidenceIncomplete fires within its `for:` window once it crosses fleet_warn_below_pct/100, confirm it clears when QGA is restored, and record the observed before/after percentages here the same way shared/storage-latency-thresholds.json's _calibration_observed does.
